rationale: Netting debt from the cash-backing leg and replacing the worst-year floor with a mean-minus-volatility reliability measure are both economically substantive changes to the archive's best performer rather than pure cosmetics, though the signal remains within the same cash-value × profitability-durability family and its incremental content over "Cash-Backed Profit Floor" may be small.

This is a one-operator swap (MA→TS_MIN on the identical conversion ratio) on an identical valuation leg from the archived "Enterprise Cash Conversion Value," i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

The stated "high and accelerating" hypothesis is not what the expression computes, since a second-difference ACCEL term is an order of magnitude smaller than the ROA level it is added to, so the quality leg collapses to plain ROA and the signal degenerates into a near-duplicate of the archived earnings-yield × profitability constructions.

Three-year cumulative operating cash flow scaled by price is a defensible smoothing of the classic cash-flow-to-price anomaly and the margin floor is a distinct conditioning variable, but the value × quality-floor template is already heavily sampled in the archive so expected incremental information is modest.

It reuses an EBITDA/EV leg that already produced negligible FF5 alpha in two archived variants, and the "high and improving" claim is undercut by adding a small DELTA term to a much larger level term, so the conditioning leg is effectively just an intangible-adjusted return level at considerable expression complexity.

Fixed-charge coverage (oibdp over interest plus depreciation) is a genuinely different conditioning dimension from the asset-scaled profitability floors already tested, the mean-minus-volatility form matches the stated "reliably cover" hypothesis, and the expected positive sign follows naturally from the construction.
